title: Human or AI?

takeaway.t: Frontier models can detect AI prose and ideas

context.t: We define a document's ideas as what its author decided to say (e.g., its claims, events, and organization), as opposed to the words used to say it (its prose).

example.source: A person wrote, in their own words, from a model's ideas

caption.t: Claude Fable 5.2 bases each decision on concrete evidence

from.title: lantern and firefly
from.src: paper/tables/minjoon-agent_attribution_examples.tex (row 1, Task cell: “Story from TwiceTold: lantern and firefly”, the title in italics); the quotation's source line

text.t: The most meaningful light is that which is provided in moments of need.
travelers to the forest always saw two lights […] the lantern never again

explanation.t: The deciding factor is the concentration of stock choices: […] and the
non-idiomatic and ungrammatical slips: “mistook greatness with size”

cases_intro.t: A document's prose and ideas can each come from a person or an AI model, giving the following four cases:

cases.def: A person wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person wrote, in their own words, from a model's ideas.
A model wrote the prose and came up with the ideas.
A person came up with the ideas, and a model wrote, rewrote, or polished the prose.
